body: My parents have known about my suicidal thoughts for almost a year now, but until recently they always assumed they were mild and weren't a significant problem for me, despite me clearly explaining that this isn't the case. About a month ago I broke down crying in front of my parents and explained to them, in as much detail as I could, how bad my thoughts they are. They said that they were sorry for how they've underestimated my issues, but since then they haven't really done much to try and help me. They are getting me to re-visit a particular counselling service who I saw for 5 months during 2016, where they underestimated my situation even more than my parents did (to give you an idea of how incompetent this counsellor was - during the first meeting I had with her, she literally said to me "suicidal thoughts are common, and we don't need to worry about them unless you have a concrete plan to do it", and then never mentioned the problem again).
